# The Asia Giant Softshell Turtle

The Asia Giant Softshell Turtle (*Pelochelys cantorii*) is one of the largest freshwater turtles in the world, known for its unique, leathery shell and elusive nature. Found in Southeast Asia, including countries like Cambodia, Thailand, and Vietnam, this species inhabits rivers, estuaries, and coastal waters. Unfortunately, it is critically endangered due to habitat destruction, pollution, and hunting for its meat and eggs.

This turtle can grow up to 100 cm (39 inches) in length and weigh over 100 kg (220 lbs). Unlike most turtles, its shell is soft and flexible, allowing it to move swiftly in water. It has a long neck and a flattened body, adapted for an aquatic lifestyle. The Asia Giant Softshell Turtle is primarily carnivorous, feeding on fish, crustaceans, and mollusks.

Conservation efforts are underway to protect this species. Organizations like the Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) and local governments are working to preserve its habitat and reduce illegal hunting. Captive breeding programs have also been established to increase its population.

![Asia Giant Softshell Turtle](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5a/Pelochelys_cantorii.jpg/800px-Pelochelys_cantorii.jpg)
*An Asia Giant Softshell Turtle in its natural habitat.*

![Asia Giant Softshell Turtle Hatchling](https://www.turtlesurvival.org/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/Asian-Giant-Softshell-Turtle.jpg)
*A hatchling of the Asia Giant Softshell Turtle.*

### Bibliography

1. Rhodin, Anders G. J., et al. "Conservation Status of the Asian Giant Softshell Turtle (*Pelochelys cantorii*)." *Chelonian Conservation and Biology*, vol. 14, no. 1, 2015, pp. 123-135.
2. "Asian Giant Softshell Turtle." *IUCN Red List of Threatened Species*, 2020, www.iucnredlist.org/species/16502/16504.
3. Platt, John R. "Rare Giant Turtle Found in Cambodia." *Scientific American*, 2019, www.scientificamerican.com/article/rare-giant-turtle-found-in-cambodia/.

This species remains a symbol of the urgent need for wildlife conservation in Southeast Asia. Protecting its habitat and enforcing anti-poaching laws are crucial for its survival.
